newsitem.title: SYRIA: Iran offers to build two cement plants in Syria.
newsitem.headline: Iran offers to build two cement plants in Syria.

text.p: Iran has offered to build two cement factories in Syria to help fill a current shortfall in production, Iranian Housing and Urban Development Minister Abbas Ahmad Akhundi said on Tuesday.
Akhundi, who co-chaired the Syrian-Iranian follow-up committee that met in Damascus for the last three days, said the deal was discussed with Syrian Prime Minister Mahmound Zu'bi.
"We offered to build two cement factories, each with a capacity of one million tonnes per year, and we had a positive response," Akhundi told Reuters.

Syria's state factories produce around five million tonnes of cement per year while local consumption exceeds seven million tonnes. Syria recently passed laws allowing the private sector into the cement industry.

Akhundi, heading a 30-member economic team, said an Iranian firm was conducting studies for the first underground train system in Damascus. Officials with the Iranian minister said the network would cover all parts of the city of three million people.
Akhundi said agreement was also reached to boost road, sea and air transport cooperation. "Iran also agreed to supply Syria with train carriages and to build a workshop to service them," he said.
The follow-up committee reports to the Supreme Commission headed by the Syrian prime minister and Iran's Vice-President Hassan Habibi.
The minister said they agreed to establish a Syrian-Iranian chamber of commerce to boost trade between the states and to open local markets.
Syrian Economy and Foreign Trade Minister Mohammed Imadi, who headed the Syrian side at the talks, said Syria agreed Iranian companies could participate in tenders for major construction projects.

He said agreement was also achieved to boost tourism between the countries. Iranian officials said over 220,000 Iranians were expected to visit Syria this year, up from about 200,000 in 1996. Iranians come to Syria mainly to visit Shi'ite shrines.
Syria has had close ties with Tehran since the Islamic revolution in 1979 and backed Iran in its war with Iraq between 1980 and 1988.
